title: Local and global finite Tor dimension on a quasi-compact pro-étale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme, meaning that every open cover of its underlying space has a finite subcover [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $A$ be a commutative ring. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with its pro-étale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a site object $U$, write $M|_U$ for derived restriction to the slice ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U,A_X|_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Derived tensor and its cohomology use [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The following are equivalent:

1. There are integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf $N$, one has $H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.
2. For every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X|_{U_i}$-module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice site, one has $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$.

No boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian, or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$, $A$, or $X$ beyond quasi-compactness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof: making local finite Tor dimension uniform on quasi-compact X; the local-to-global argument applies to arbitrary constant coefficient module complexes. Local finite Tor dimension is Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, in sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text: Restrict a bounded flat coefficient model along the exact slice restriction. The coefficient-sized flat-model criterion, exactness and preservation of finite limits and colimits give a bounded flat model with the same strict degree bounds; the restricted model is flat and its derived-category factorization is transported by the restriction functor.

source.place: Tags 03DH and 08H5: exact localization restriction preserves the bounded flat Tor model.

proof.text: For a K-flat global test complex, exact K-flat restriction and the natural slice tensor isomorphism identify the restricted global tensor homology with the tensor homology in the slice. Applying the local amplitude hypothesis therefore makes every out-of-interval restricted homology object zero.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 08FZ and 0E8K: tensor restriction, K-flat restriction and Tor-amplitude vanishing.

proof.text: For the converse, use the terminal object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Quasi-compactness and the affine pro-etale refinement give a finite cover subordinate to the local presieve. The covering-top criterion at a terminal object extends this to every site object. Taking the minimum of all lower bounds and zero, and the maximum of all upper bounds and zero, gives a common interval. Sectionwise zero detection for a sheaf over this finite cover then proves the global amplitude condition.

source.place: Tags 0989, 098B and 09C2: finite affine refinement and the uniform Tor interval.

from.place: Proof of det-lem-integral-models-stacks: identification of local finite Tor dimension in Stacks 09C1 with a global finite Tor interval; expanded uniformity sentence in Stacks 09C2.

split_report.summary: Preserved the arbitrary constant-coefficient statement. Proved both implications using the existing ringed-site Tor restriction theorem, exact restriction and derived tensor comparison. Uniformized bounds on finite affine refinements and proved global vanishing directly from the sheaf axiom, including the empty scheme. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes det-lem-integral-models-stacks, proof step identifying locally finite Tor dimension of the first residue reduction with a single global Tor interval, expanding the uniformity sentence of Stacks 09C2 on the integral-models route.

tool_uses.why: Its arbitrary-ringed-topos tensor comparison specializes to localization; the integral-models unit does not supply this general tensor identity.
Its arbitrary-ringed-site statement preserves a fixed interval against every slice module, for both global-to-local and refinement; the unit gives no such general restriction theorem.
The pro-etale topology, including finite affine refinement for affine targets and Zariski covers, supplies the covering facts used to uniformize bounds without a Noetherian hypothesis.

Its K-flat flat-term model of the ringed-site derived tensor identifies the tensor of the cited Tor restriction theorem with the Tor-amplitude tensor of the statement; the integral-models unit gives no tensor convention of its own.
